terms.definition: Characteristic energy: the square of the speed left over once a spacecraft has escaped the Earth, in km²/s² — the figure a launcher must reach for a given trip.

terms.name: delta-v
terms.definition: Change in velocity, written Δv: how much a spacecraft can change its motion, the currency of every mission plan, in km/s.

terms.definition: The way down to a surface, from orbit or from the atmosphere to touchdown.

terms.name: entry
terms.definition: A spacecraft's passage into a planet's atmosphere, where drag and heating slow it down.

terms.name: exoplanet
terms.definition: A planet that orbits a star other than the Sun; more than 5,000 are known, most found by the dip in light as they cross their star.

terms.definition: A close pass by a planet, moon or other body without going into orbit around it or landing.

terms.name: free-return
terms.definition: A path to the Moon that swings round its far side and falls back to Earth with no further burn, so a crew can come home even if the engine fails.

terms.name: geostationary
terms.definition: The circular orbit 35,786 km above the equator in which a satellite goes round once a day and so stays over the same spot on the ground.

terms.definition: The range of distances from a star where a planet could keep liquid water on its surface: not too hot, not too cold.

terms.name: halo orbit
terms.definition: A looping orbit around a Lagrange point, held there by the balance of two bodies' gravity — JWST circles one at L2, Gateway was planned for another.

terms.name: heat shield
terms.definition: The layer that protects a spacecraft from the heat of atmospheric entry, usually by charring and wearing away.

terms.definition: The cheapest way between two circular orbits: one burn onto half an ellipse that touches both, and a second burn to circularise at the far end.

terms.name: inclination
